newsitem.title: USA: EXEL in strategic review of businesses.
newsitem.headline: EXEL in strategic review of businesses.

text.p: EXEL Ltd said on Tuesday it is close to completing the first phase of a strategic review of its businesses launched earlier this year.

In the first phase of the review, the company is examining its strategic initiatives and customer focus as it seeks out potentially new ways to grow in an increasingly competitive environment, EXEL spokesman Gavin Arton said.
EXEL was a "phenomenally successful company in its first 10 years," he said.
But now "we are entering a period of more intense competition," he said.

"Top line revenues were reflecting the impact of business erosion and cheap pricing and we felt we want to be a growth company and the ways to grow have to be, perhaps, different than they were in the first decade," he said.
Phase two of the review will involve the implementation of the initiatives and the third phase will involve an assessment of the success of those measures, he said.
The entire review is expected to take about three years.

The company does not expect to make any sweeping announcement about the new initiatives planned and said some of the changes may simply involve adjustments to the company's day-to-day, behind-the-scenes operations.
Some of the focus will be on ways to improve distribution as the insurance brokerage industry undergoes a major consolidation, he said.
But Arton said the review was more of an "evolution, not revolution."
EXEL chief executive Brian O'Hara also cited the company's recent purchase of Global Capital Holdings Ltd.

"As demonstrated by our recent purchase of Global Capital Holdings Ltd, we have identified several opportunities for selective expansion of our insurance and financial services businesses," O'Hara said in a statement.
EXEL on Tuesday reported second quarter operating earnings of $0.99 a share, topping the First Call estimate of $0.89.
The company reported operating earnings of $0.78 a share in the year ago second quarter.
Although earnings increased, net premiums written declined to $64.3 million compared with $143.8 million in the 1996 second quarter.

After adjusting for premiums relating to multi-year contracts and the impact of specialty reinsurance assumed TRIPLICAT policies, net premiums increased 24 percent to $102.1 million in the 1997 second quarter from $82.2 million a year ago.
